# Intro to ggplot

## What is it?

- R package that implements Cleveland's "grammar of graphics"
  - Written by Hadley Wickham, CTO of Posit.co
- Map data to figure components
  - Position
  - Color, shape, size
- Add layers to figures

## Why 'code' your figures?

- Easier to reproduce
- Easier to edit
- Try out different styles, pick the best
- Be kind to your future (forgetful) self
- Makes programming more fun

## Installing ggplot

- Open RStudio
- Enter the following in your R console

```r
install.packages("ggplot2")
```

## Let's make some data


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
days <- factor(
  c("sun", "mon", "tue", "wed", "thu", "fri", "sat"),
  levels = c("sun", "mon", "tue", "wed", "thu", "fri", "sat"),
  ordered = TRUE
)
meals <- factor(
  c("breakfast", "lunch", "dinner", "snack", "dessert"),
  levels = c("breakfast", "lunch", "snack", "dinner", "dessert"),
  ordered = TRUE
)
meal_days <- rep(days, each = length(meals))
weekly_meals <- rep(meals, 7)

my_meals <- data.frame(day_of_wk = meal_days, 
                       meal = weekly_meals)
```
:::


## Let's make some data

- I created a new `ate_skipped` variable
- This let's me create a new logical variable called `ate` that is `TRUE` if `ate_skipped == TRUE`


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ate_skipped <- sample(c("ate", "skipped"), size = 35, 
                 replace = TRUE, prob = c(.6, .4))
ate <- ate_skipped == "ate"
ate
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
 [1]  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE  TRUE
[13]  TRUE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE FALSE
[25]  TRUE FALSE FALSE  TRUE FALSE FALSE  TRUE FALSE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE
```


:::
:::


## Let's make some data

- Why do this?
- It makes it easy to assign a NA value to all of the ratings where `ate==FALSE`


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ratings <- sample(c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5), size = 35,
                 replace = TRUE)

ratings[ate == FALSE] <- NA
```
:::


## Let's make some data


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
my_meals$ate_skipped <- ate_skipped
my_meals$rating <- ratings
```
:::

## Figure 0

::: {.callout-note}
This is a simple `ggplot2` figure using data already available in R.

Click on the arrow to view the code.

The rendered figure is on the next slide.
:::


::: {.cell output-location='slide'}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(data = airquality) + 
  aes(x = Temp, y = Ozone) +
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](include/fig/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){width=960}
:::
:::


## Figure 1.0

::: {.question}
## How many meals were eaten vs. skipped?
:::


::: {.cell output-location='slide'}

```{.r .cell-code  code-line-numbers="1|2|3|4"}
my_meals |> 
  ggplot() + 
  aes(x = ate_skipped) + 
  geom_bar() 
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![A barplot of meals eaten and skipped.](include/fig/fig-barplot-ate_skipped-1.png){#fig-barplot-ate_skipped width=960}
:::
:::


---

::: {.callout-important}
## Nominal data often require processing before plotting

This is most often a count of the number of instances per category.
It could be the relative proportion, but this is calculated from the number of instances.
:::

## Figure 1.1

- Add a `fill` aesthetic to fill the bars with colors 


::: {.cell output-location='slide'}

```{.r .cell-code  code-line-numbers="|3"}
my_meals |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = ate_skipped, fill = ate_skipped) +
  geom_bar()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![A barplot of meals eaten and skipped.](include/fig/fig-barplot-ate_skipped-fill-1.png){#fig-barplot-ate_skipped-fill width=960}
:::
:::


::: {.fragment}
- If we fill from `ate_skipped`
  - ggplot will map a color to each distinct value of `ate_skipped`
  - and add a legend, so we know what the colors represent
  
:::

## Figure 2.0

::: {.question}
## What is the distribution of meal ratings?

::: {.cell output-location='slide'}

```{.r .cell-code  code-line-numbers="|2"}
ggplot(data = my_meals) + 
  aes(x = rating) +
  geom_bar()
```

## Basic ggplot components

- A data frame
- Function call to `ggplot()`
- Add layers to plot with `+` operator
- Add aesthetics (mappings between data and graphic elements) using `aes()` with x (and often y) mappings
- A `geom_` layer

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
